newsitem.title: USA: Cargo plane crashes at Miami airport.
newsitem.headline: Cargo plane crashes at Miami airport.

text.p: A Fine Air DC-8 cargo plane crashed seconds after takeoff from Miami International Airport on Thursday, ploughing across a roadway and scattering flaming wreckage through a busy warehouse district.
Witnesses said one of the plane's engines appeared to have caught fire in the air, sending the jet into a nosedive just off the end of one of the airport's runways.
There were no immediate reports of injuries but the fate of the four-person crew was uncertain, police said.
The Federal Aviation Administration said the plane, Fine Air Flight 101, was headed to Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic.
"I have no information on the fate of the crew," FAA spokesman Eliot Brenner said.

Burning wreckage was scattered across a busy roadway and a parking lot, sending a towering column of thick black smoke into the air that was visible from downtown Miami, more than 10 miles (16 km) away.
"It dropped like a rock -- boom -- right out of the sky," witness George Foch said. "It must have been in flight two minutes tops. It was incredible. It just dropped."
The aircraft took off at 12:34 p.m. EDT (1634 GMT) and went down moments later in clear weather. Fire crews poured fire retardant chemicals over the wreckage.
The crash stunned hundreds of workers in the busy commercial district just west of Miami International Airport.
Bill Garcia, who was on the picket line at a UPS facility in the area, echoed other witnesses who said one of the plane's engines appeared to have caught fire in the air.
"All of a sudden it veered to the right, then to the left, we could see an engine on fire, then it nosedived," he said. "It looked like a missile."
Fine Air Services Inc's initial public offering of stock hit the NASDAQ market on Wednesday.
